title: Report
description: One LSD report: its scenarios, each with a sequence diagram's participants and events. Written by lsd-mono-jvm as <stem>-report.json, and as window.__LSD_REPORT__ in the diagram page. Pre-1.0: may change before 1.0.0. The compatibility rule: readers ignore fields they do not know, and a minor version (0.x included, 1.x alike) only adds optional fields, values of open enums and event kinds. Objects accept properties they do not list, and the open enums (see each one) accept values they do not list, so this schema still validates a report of a newer minor version. status is the worst scenario status: error, then warn, then success; success when there are no scenarios.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the report follows: semver, apart from the lsd-mono version. 0.3.0 for this schema.

generatedAt.description: When the report was written: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. lsd-mono-jvm writes UTC with Z, to the millisecond or less (the seconds alone when they are whole).

generator.description: The producer and its version, such as `lsd-mono 0.7.0`. The usage ping matches this text, so it does not change shape.

Status.title: Status
Status.description: A scenario's or report's outcome, in lower case.

ParticipantType.title: ParticipantType
ParticipantType.description: How a participant is drawn. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers draw a type they do not know as PARTICIPANT.

MessageType.title: MessageType
MessageType.description: How a message's arrow is drawn. SHORT_INBOUND comes in from the diagram's edge and SHORT_OUTBOUND leaves to it. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers draw a type they do not know as a SYNCHRONOUS arrow.

TimingSource.title: TimingSource
TimingSource.description: Where a message's duration came from. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers show a value they do not know as it is.

PairingSource.title: PairingSource
PairingSource.description: How a reply was paired with its call. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers treat a value they do not know as NONE.

OrderSource.title: OrderSource
OrderSource.description: What put a message where it is. CLOCK: moved by clock ordering (startedAt), shown with a badge. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers treat a value they do not know as SEQUENCE.

WarningKind.title: WarningKind
WarningKind.description: What a timing warning is about; the Timing view labels its pill from it. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers show a kind they do not know with its message only.

Accuracy.title: Accuracy
Accuracy.description: Optional on a scenario; see Scenario for the default.

ClockOrdering.title: ClockOrdering
ClockOrdering.description: Optional on a scenario; default SAME_SOURCE.

ReportSource.title: ReportSource
ReportSource.description: The integration that wrote the report, counted by the usage ping. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers treat a value they do not know as no known source (the usage ping counts no source).

ReportOptions.title: ReportOptions

metricsEnabled.description: When false, every scenario's metrics are empty. Default true.

labelMaxWidth.description: Characters diagram labels and metric summaries are cut to. Default 200.

usagePing.description: Whether the page may request the usage ping files: at most one fire-and-forget request per event, whose failure is ignored. The page also needs a release generator. Default true, as lsd-mono writes it: on unless lsd.mono.report.usagePing=false. Unlike the other fields, a missing value is read as false, so a report that does not say is never pinged.

ReportOptions.description: Settings the producer wrote the report with. Optional, as is each field: a reader uses the default each field names.

ScenarioError.title: ScenarioError
ScenarioError.description: Why a failed or aborted scenario did not pass.

stack.description: Absent when the producer hid stack traces. Shown in the inspector as text.

Fact.title: Fact
Fact.description: A key fact shown on the scenario card.

Metric.title: Metric
Metric.description: A metric line. Absent when metrics are off.

PairAccuracy.title: PairAccuracy
PairAccuracy.description: The accuracy of the messages between two participants.

from.description: Sender id; an empty string for the diagram's edge, as on a message.

to.description: Receiver id; an empty string for the diagram's edge, as on a message.

alias.description: The participant's display name (displayName in the Kotlin API), drawn instead of name. Absent when it has none.

colour.description: A CSS colour for the participant's header.

attributes.description: Facts about the participant, such as the service it is (service.name, service.version, service.namespace) or the remote service it stands for (peer.service).

Trace.title: Trace
Trace.description: Trace context on a message, in OpenTelemetry's terms, and frozen at these three ids: no minor version adds to it, and anything more about the span (trace flags, trace state, span kind, status) goes in the message's attributes. Ids are as the producer received them; lsd-mono-jvm never invents them. W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry write lowercase hex, 32 characters for traceId and 16 for spanId and parentSpanId, and a producer should write them that way. B3 ids are accepted too, including a 16-character (64-bit) traceId, so no format is enforced.

traceId.description: The trace: 32 lowercase hex characters (W3C, OpenTelemetry), or 16 or 32 for B3.

spanId.description: This message's span: 16 lowercase hex characters. A reply with its call's spanId is paired with it.

parentSpanId.description: The span this one runs inside: 16 lowercase hex characters. Nests the message inside the call with that spanId.

MessageOrigin.title: MessageOrigin
MessageOrigin.description: Where a message came from: captured, recorded by the producer while the test ran (as lsd-mono-jvm does), or imported, built afterwards from another record, such as OpenTelemetry spans from a file or a trace backend. Absent means captured. Not the same as source, the message's clock domain. Open: a newer producer may send a value not listed here. Readers show a value they do not know as it is.

AttributeValue.title: AttributeValue
AttributeValue.description: One attribute's value, as OpenTelemetry's are: a string, a boolean, a number, or a list of one of those.

Attributes.title: Attributes
Attributes.description: Facts about a message or a participant as named keys, such as a message's HTTP route or messaging destination, or the service a participant is. Keys use OpenTelemetry semantic convention names where there is one (http.request.method, http.route, http.response.status_code, url.full, messaging.destination.name, rpc.method; service.name, service.version, peer.service), and keys starting lsd. are kept for lsd-mono's own. Keys are not empty. Absent, rather than empty, when there are none. Readers show or ignore them; no attribute changes how a message or participant is drawn.

MessageEvent.title: MessageEvent
MessageEvent.description: A message between two participants. data is its payload: any JSON value, absent when it has none. In the diagram page's copy, when payloadId is set, only the payload's method, path and status (or nothing) stay in data.

from.description: Sender id. An empty string, not an absent field, for a diagram edge: SHORT_INBOUND.

to.description: Receiver id. An empty string, not an absent field, for a diagram edge: SHORT_OUTBOUND.

durationMs.description: Milliseconds, to the microsecond, without trailing zeros.

payloadId.description: Key into the payload sidecar (<scenarioId>/<messageId>), set in the diagram page's copy when the payload loads on open. Never in <stem>-report.json.

seq.description: Capture order. Absent when not counted.

replyTo.description: On a reply: the call it answers.

causedBy.description: On a consume: the publish that caused it.

source.description: Clock domain, such as a service name. Absent means local.

capturedAt.description: Wall-clock time of capture. Left out of reproducible reports.

status.description: The message's status, such as an HTTP status, as text even when it is a number.

parentId.description: Id of the call this message runs inside, as the library nested it (span link, else innermost open call).

replyOf.description: On a paired reply: id of the call it answers.

startedAt.description: When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.

over.description: Anchor participant. Set for placement over; optional for left and right.

startedAt.description: When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.

DividerEvent.title: DividerEvent
DividerEvent.description: A labelled line across the diagram.

startedAt.description: When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.

SectionEvent.title: SectionEvent
SectionEvent.description: A titled row in one continuous diagram. Does not split the drawing or end activations.

startedAt.description: When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.
When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.
When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.

ActivateEvent.title: ActivateEvent
ActivateEvent.description: Starts or ends a participant's activation bar.

colour.description: Activation bar colour. Only on activate, and only when the caller set one.

startedAt.description: When it started, by its source's clock: an RFC 3339 date-time, with Z or a UTC offset. Events are sorted by it before layout when any event in the list has one.

UnknownEvent.title: UnknownEvent
UnknownEvent.description: An event of a kind this version does not know, from a newer producer. Event kinds are open: readers drop an event of a kind they do not know.

DiagramEvent.title: DiagramEvent
DiagramEvent.description: One row of a sequence diagram, by kind. The generated TypeScript type leaves out UnknownEvent: the report UI drops those when it loads a report.
DiagramEvent.tsType: MessageEvent | NoteEvent | DividerEvent | SectionEvent | DelayEvent | SpacerEvent | ActivateEvent

Scenario.title: Scenario
Scenario.description: One scenario: a test or a feature's scenario. The timing summary (accuracy to pairAccuracy) sits flat on the scenario, not in an object of its own. accuracy says how the scenario's timings were captured. The timing summary (accuracy, sources, clockOrdering, clockOrdered and the optional fields after them) is optional for a producer without timing analysis. A reader's defaults: accuracy MEASURED when a message has a duration or start time, else STRUCTURE_ONLY; sources as described; clockOrdering SAME_SOURCE; clockOrdered 0.

description.description: Plain text; Given, When, Then and And lines are highlighted.

measuredCoverage.description: Share of calls with a measured duration, 0 to 1. Absent when there are no calls.

pairingCoverage.description: Share of calls paired with their reply by call id or trace, 0 to 1. Absent when there are no calls.

sources.description: Distinct clock domains of the messages, local included (local is the name for a message with no source). Optional: a reader's default is ["local"] when the scenario has messages, else [].

wallClockMs.description: From the first start to the last end. Only for a single clock domain whose measured calls all have a start. Milliseconds, to the microsecond, without trailing zeros.

clockOrdered.description: How many messages clock ordering placed. Default 0.

warnings.description: Absent, rather than empty, when there are none.

reorderedByClock.description: Ids of the messages clock ordering moved. Absent, rather than empty, when there are none.

pairAccuracy.description: Accuracy per participant pair, present only when the pairs differ.
